content: Hi everyone,I would like to sincerely apologize for my previous posts. I realize now that my approach was too informal and that the code snippets I provided lacked the necessary context and mathematical rigour for this community. I am a researcher working on Dual Sets Theory (DST), and I am learning how to use Lean 4 to provide a verified foundation for my work. During my time away, I have started refactoring my project from the ground up, moving away from high-level claims to a strict bottom-up axiomatic approach. What I have done so far:Axioms 0-1: Defined the DST_Space structure representing the "Vault" (universal set) and the basic involution operator $\iota$. Axiom 2: Formalized the involution property ($\iota(\iota(x)) = x$) to ensure information conservation. Formal Proof: Successfully proved the uniqueness of duality (Axiom 02) as a theorem within the DST structure. My goal is not to present a "final solution," but to build a solid foundation where each step—from logic to number theory and biological stability—is verified. You can find the new foundational code here: https://github.com/toshiro881967-coder/DST-Vault (specifically in DstVault/Foundations.lean). I would appreciate any feedback on whether this structure-based approach is the most efficient way to represent an involutive theory in Lean 4.Thank you for your patience and for the work you do for the Lean ecosystem.Best regards,Francesco
